item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 110525
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Sun Oct 11 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The Weather Prediction Center is issuing advisories on
Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias, located inland over Tennessee.

Eastern Tropical Atlantic:
An elongated area of low pressure centered about 100 miles
southwest of the Cabo Verde Islands is producing a large but
disorganized area of showers and thunderstorms extending from
near those islands southward for several hundred miles. Some
development of this system is possible during the next couple of
days while the low north-northwestward before upper-level winds
become too strong for development by midweek. Very heavy rainfall
is also possible during the next few days over portions of the Cabo
Verde Islands regardless of whether the system ever becomes a
tropical cyclone.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Summary for Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias (AT4/AL092026)
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...FLASH FLOODING RISK CONTINUES ALONG BLUE RIDGE AS ISAIAS STARTS ACCELERATION NORTHEASTWARD... As of 4:00 AM CDT Sun Oct 11 the center of Isaias was located near 35.4, -85.9 with movement NE at 23 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1010 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 25 mph.

item.title: Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias Forecast Discussion Number 19
item.description:
Issued at 400 AM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026 
000
WTNT44 KWNH 110834
TCDAT4
 
Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias Discussion Number  19
NWS Weather Prediction Center College Park MD   AL092026
400 AM CDT Sun Oct 11 2026
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Post-Tropical Cyclone Isaias will 
spread into the Central Appalachians and Mid-Atlantic on Sunday.  
Isolated flash and urban flooding will be possible.
 
2. Strong wind gusts continue to pose a threat across the
southeastern United States today, particularly near the southern
Appalachians. Scattered power outages and downed trees and
power-lines may occur, with the risk highest in elevated terrain.
 
3. Swells from Isaias will continue to affect much of the Gulf and 
Southeastern Atlantic coasts of the United States, Mexico, and 
western Cuba this weekend. These swells are likely to cause 
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult 
products from your local weather office.
 
4. A couple of tornadoes are possible today across the Piedmont and 
Coastal Plain of Virginia and North Carolina.
